text:
anya: idea — instead of storing full provenance on the compact path, emit a tiny verifiable "proof" at ingest: claim_id + fingerprint + key_id. makes compacts cheap and auditable without heavy IO.
ben: sounds promising. fingerprint = deterministic hash over request meta? e.g. sha256(model, tenant, root_id, token_counts) then HMAC?
anya: yep. HMAC with gateway key. proof size ~128-256b, index-friendly. claim_id derived deterministically from root_request_id + shard + seq so retries/dedup are stable.
carla: main operational risk is out-of-order arrival: compact write before provenance. how do we patch?
dima: mark compact rows as "unresolved" with short TTL (e.g., 30m) and a tombstone marker in the compact index. on provenance arrival we patch fields. if no provenance after TTL, enqueue record for full-rehydrate in audit pipeline.
ravi: billing needs absolute determinism. enrichment must never alter claim_id mapping or token attribution semantics.
anya: agreed. billing should always use (claim_id, fingerprint) as authoritative keys. enrichment only populates display fields (model_version, prompt_hash, token_breakdown).
ben: ops Q: gateway HMAC key rotation — auditors need to validate old proofs. how do we handle historical keys?
carla: include key_id in the proof. provenance service maintains rotation table and archived keys for at least audit_retention + margin. validation uses key_id to select historical key.
dima: perf concern: computing sha256+HMAC on hot path per request may add CPU. we should benchmark. if it's heavy, consider a tiny sidecar batcher for HMAC ops.
ravi: or a specialized SIMD implementation in the gateway runtime. bench first.
anya: minimal proof schema proposal (compact JSON shown inline so it's searchable):

```json
{
  "claim_id": "str",
  "fingerprint": "hex",
  "key_id": "str",
  "ts": "epoch_ms",
  "flags": ["compact"]
}
```

carla: okay shape. add three metrics: compact_unresolved_count, compact_patched_count, compact_fallback_rehydrates. also expose histograms for patch_latency.
dima: backfill policy: if provenance arrives after TTL, emit a backfill/audit event with rehydrate_hint. consumers must be idempotent keyed by claim_id. include a small sequence number to detect flips.
anya: consumer dedupe by claim_id + sequence. sequence increments on retry handshakes.
ben: can we reuse chunked-handshake endpoints? I'd prefer reusing the existing handshake contract with mode=compact. reduces new surface.
anya: yep reuse is my preference too, handshake API already supports small payloads. add mode toggle and opt-in flag per tenant.
ravi: rollout: default off, pilot internal tenants, measure storage delta and audit false-positive rate. connect Redwood Optimize to detect attribution drift.
carla: add required tests: gateway unit tests for HMAC generation and verification, integration tests for patch flows, chaos test simulating late provenance and double-writes.
metering-bot: note: open ENG-XXXX perf ticket for HMAC bench, and ENG-YYYY key-rotation playbook. Ensure retention policy for historical keys >= audit window + 30d.
anya: i'll write a RFC follow-up doc w/bench-plan, perf targets, failure modes, schema, and rollout checklist. will link this convo.
ben: small ask — log claim_id -> ingest_node and claim_id -> gateway_key_id for debugging.
dima: also add an internal-only debug endpoint to force patch replays for a claim_id to simplify post-mortem drills.
ravi: I'll run a 20k-sample synthetic run on a gateway + sidecar prototype and post CPU/latency profiles.
anya: TL;DR tradeoffs: compact proofs reduce storage and read IO and speed common queries, but increase complexity for enrichment/backfill, depend on key-rotation safety and idempotent consumers. next: RFC follow-up + perf + tests. thanks.
